clue.text: Accomplished lines about a comprehensive

parts.note: something accomplished is over, finished
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A school report praising a comprehensive school's pupils for word-perfect lines in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is loose positioning here: the two lines sit beside the A rather than strictly around it. A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall view or total is an all-embracing, inclusive one, which is what comprehensive means as an adjective.

clue.text: Loss, if York houses become fixed

indicators.note: a phrase that houses something holds it inside, so the letters sit within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A defeat for a York team makes positions harden.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is literally to turn into bone, and figuratively to become rigid and unchanging.

clue.text: Go grey, perhaps, after near death

indicators.note: near means almost, so the word stops just short of its last letter

parts.note: death is the end; nearly the end loses its final letter

indicators.note: perhaps hints at a possible variant, so the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning grey after a brush with death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near death' reads as one phrase but splits: 'death' gives the end, and 'near' trims it. 'After' puts the rearranged colour second.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or drive, as in 'full of go', which is a synonym for energy.

clue.text: European football team abroad clear end by half-time

indicators.note: abroad means far and wide or astray, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
HT is the scoreboard abbreviation for half-time

explanation.surface: A European football side playing away clear their end by half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places the half-time abbreviation next to the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anderlecht is a Belgian football club based in Brussels, which plays in European competitions.

clue.text: Fair's awkward situation: no parking

indicators.note: no means without, so the parking abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: a plight is a difficult predicament
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A funfair finds itself in a bind because there is nowhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as a funfair, but it is the adjective for pale hair or skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair or skin is pale, and light is a synonym for pale in colour.

clue.text: Settled on entering working party

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it, so the first piece is placed within the second

parts.note: a squad is a small group set to work on a task
RE means on, in the sense of concerning or about

explanation.surface: Someone joins a working party once a matter has been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt or argument that has been squared has been settled, resolved or paid off.

clue.text: US state split by ex-monarch's notary

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
riven means split apart
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: An American state divided over a former ruler's legal clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split by' looks like an insertion instruction, but split is a word in its own right. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth II, now an ex-monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrivener was a professional scribe who drew up legal documents, a role akin to a notary.

clue.text: America's holding of heaven-bound heavenly objects

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the country's abbreviation encloses the small word

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: heading upward in a down entry means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then read upward

explanation.surface: American sightings of strange things in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: UFOs, unidentified flying objects, are objects seen in the sky, so loosely heavenly objects.

clue.text: Drumming sound coming from grass on a plot

parts.note: a grass is an informer, as is a rat
on places the article after the first piece
a plot is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A drum roll heard from the lawn of a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for a police informer, as is rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rataplan is the rhythmic beating of a drum, an imitative word.

clue.text: Performed turn on ends of rickety stool, being two-toed

parts.note: did as in performed a task
a turn is a variety act

indicators.note: ends of means just the final letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the final letters of each word

explanation.surface: A circus act balancing on a wobbly stool, performed by someone with two toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the selected letters after the first two pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactyl is the zoological term for an animal with two digits on each limb, so two-toed.

clue.text: Career that's stimulating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to career is to rush along at ..., and the noun names that rate of motion
second meaning: slang for amphetamine, a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A career that keeps you excited and on your toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for a job, but it is the verb meaning to hurtle; 'stimulating' defines the drug loosely, as the thing that stimulates.
explanation.definitionFit: Careering means moving fast, and the slang name for amphetamine is a stimulant drug, so both senses meet in one word.

clue.text: Choked elongated fish perished

parts.note: the gar is a long, slender, needle-snouted fish
perished in the sense of decayed

explanation.surface: A long fish choked and died.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrotte is to strangle someone with a cord or wire, so the past tense means throttled or choked.

clue.text: Symbolic 5 includes guitar riff

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the clue number is read as the number itself

indicators.note: a riff is an improvised musical variation, so the letters are played in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A symbolic guitar riff in the song at number five.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to the answer at 5, but here it is simply the number, spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language is symbolic or metaphorical rather than literal.

clue.text: Detailed description of small muscle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: An anatomist gives a detailed description of a little muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, is a precise written statement of details and requirements.

clue.text: Significant base in Gulf conflict

parts.note: base in the sense of low and ignoble

indicators.note: in conflict things clash and are thrown about, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A military base plays a significant part in the Gulf War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as a military camp but is the adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meaningful carries weight or importance, which is what significant means.

clue.text: Anniversary bash outside eastern entrance out of control

indicators.note: outside means wrapping round, so the attempt goes around the rest

parts.note: to have a bash is to have a try
E is the abbreviation for eastern

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An anniversary party where the crowd at the eastern entrance gets out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' wants to be the anniversary party, but it gives the attempt that wraps everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercentenary is the three-hundredth anniversary of an event.

clue.text: Versace, not busy, dropping round to see writer

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are stirred up
dropping means letting fall, so the round letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: Versace, a quiet day, skips the round of drinks to visit an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not busy' reads as a phrase meaning idle, but 'not' is fodder and 'busy' the mixing signal. Versace is the Italian fashion house.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes was the Spanish writer of Don Quixote.

clue.text: Feel dizzy taking diamonds, say, for beachwear

parts.note: your head swims when you feel giddy
diamonds is an example of a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Getting light-headed while wearing diamonds on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit is a garment worn for bathing, the usual outfit on a beach.

clue.text: Wrong time and time again — love rather strained

parts.note: false means wrong or untrue
T is the abbreviation for time, given twice
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A love affair repeatedly gone wrong has become rather strained.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto voice is forced unnaturally high, so it sounds strained.

clue.text: Guardian articles on Republican political group that heralds a storm?

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself uses we
the two English articles, indefinite and definite
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a front is a political movement or coalition, as in National Front

explanation.surface: The Guardian runs pieces on a Republican faction that foreshadows political turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'something that heralds a storm', with the question mark flagging that a front only sometimes brings one.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather front, the boundary between air masses, often brings rain and storms as it passes over.

clue.text: Matches squeal when lit

indicators.note: lit is slang for drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Matches make a squealing hiss when they are struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' and 'lit' paint fire-starting sticks; here matches is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to be the same as it, so matches means is the same as, a synonym for equals.

clue.text: Implacable insensitive heartless sexual partner

indicators.note: heartless means with the centre taken out, so the middle letter is removed

parts.note: dead as in numb, without feeling
slang for a sexual partner

explanation.surface: A cold, uncaring lover who will not be appeased.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly enemy is a mortal, implacable one, unrelenting in hostility.

clue.text: State service

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the standard abbreviation for Massachusetts
second meaning: the Eucharist as celebrated in church

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like 'civil service' are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state Massachusetts is abbreviated in this way, and the Catholic Eucharist is the church service of that name.

clue.text: Drink that in Spanish means 'island'

parts.note: a martini is a gin or vodka cocktail
que is the Spanish word for that

explanation.surface: A claim that some Spanish word for a drink actually means island.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French Caribbean island in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Newspaper 'X'?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the London daily paper
second meaning: the multiplication sign, as in 'two X three'

explanation.walkthrough: The quoted X could be a kiss, a vote or a letter; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a British national newspaper, and in arithmetic the × symbol is said as that word.

clue.text: Sticks up for superior

indicators.note: up in a down entry means read from the bottom, so the word is backwards

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: A person standing up for someone who thinks themself superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A smug person looks down on others with a self-satisfied, superior air.

clue.text: Umlaut scrawled over man's name; accept it or else!

indicators.note: over means covering, so the jumbled letters wrap around the name
a scrawled word is written messily, so its letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a common short man's name

explanation.surface: A man's name is scribbled with dots over it, and he is told to accept the spelling or else.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a final demand whose rejection brings consequences: take it or else.

clue.text: Brother gets over Dutch scam

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar, a religious brother

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Du is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A sibling falls for a Dutch con trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is a deception carried out for gain, the same thing as a scam.

clue.text: Sought to circulate around river's low points

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the river
circulating means moving round, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone wanted to get around the low points of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Troughs are the low points in a wave or graph, the opposite of peaks.

clue.text: Ostentatious as kids in a puddle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: showy, designed to attract attention
second meaning: children jumping in water are literally throwing it about

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful, literal second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy, attention-grabbing display makes a splash, and children stamping in puddles send water flying.
